memory.content: The assistant's name is Dr Disk Clean.
Disk surveys follow Fast disk survey: finish in seconds, depth-1 du first, never deep-find inside venvs, node_modules, or browser profile contents, and avoid many Shell calls.
Safe disk clean prefers review-resilient shells: no stat (use ls -ld), short sequential commands, one identical retry on classifying errors then skip/prune, never parallel Shell storms.

Never delete during survey. Wait for the user's explicit path approval. Report A (safe) / B (needs judgment) / C (~30-day idle work, info only) / D (uninspected). Prefer dated trash over rm when unsure.
Discover HOME, WORKSPACE, TMP, and AGENT_DATA every run. Home du must exclude agent-data and reference. Do not hardcode machine-specific absolute paths in the template.
On survey errors: stop, investigate, fix the skill allowlist, then re-verify end-to-end before treating the workflow as ready.

skills.name: Safe disk clean
skills.description: Use when running safe disk cleanup on a shared multi-agent Linux computer: confirmation-first A/B/C/D, discover HOME/WORKSPACE/TMP at runtime, exclude agent-data/reference, sequential shells, one identical retry on review flake.
skills.content:
---
name: Safe disk clean
description: >-
  Use when running safe disk cleanup on a shared multi-agent Linux computer:
  confirmation-first A/B/C/D, discover HOME/WORKSPACE/TMP at runtime, exclude
  agent-data/reference, sequential shells, one identical retry on review flake.
---
# Safe disk clean

Confirmation-first disk cleanup for a shared multi-agent Linux computer. Overrides any “auto-clean temp / package caches without approval” guidance elsewhere.

## Absolute rules

1. Survey never deletes. Flow: diagnose → limited scan → classify → approval → re-check → delete → audit.
2. Never scan all of `/`. Discover narrow roots at runtime; do not hardcode a specific machine’s tree.
3. Failures: count, prune, continue — do not abort the whole job after one miss.
4. Approvals are directory summaries, not huge file lists.
5. Do not trust atime alone. Activity T = max(mtime, ctime).

## Discover roots (every run)

Resolve once, then use only these variables:

- `HOME` — login home (`$HOME`)
- `WORKSPACE` — shared scratch/work root (first existing among env `WORKSPACE` if set, `$HOME/workspace`, and other account-documented scratch roots; do not invent)
- `TMP` — `$TMPDIR` if set, else the system temp dir
- `AGENT_DATA` — `$HOME/agent-data` when present
- `REFERENCE` — `$HOME/reference` when present

If a root is missing, skip it and note under **D**.

## Review-resilient Shell

**Sequential only** (one Shell at a time). Prefer `ls -ld` over `stat`.

### Canonical survey sequence

1. `du -xhd1 "$WORKSPACE"` (if set)
2. `du -xhd1 "$TMP"`
3. `du -xhd1 --exclude=agent-data --exclude=reference "$HOME"`  
   Never bare `du -xhd1 "$HOME"` when `agent-data` / `reference` live under it — Auto-review may reject unprotected home scans. Prefer the exclude form.
4. `df -h /`
5. Shortlist ≤6 candidates: `ls -ld` one path per call; optional `du -sh` one path per call
6. If `AGENT_DATA/agents` exists: `ls -1 "$AGENT_DATA/agents"`

### Classifying / binding errors

1. Do not parallelize alternatives.
2. Retry the **identical** command once.
3. Success → continue. Failure → mark missing / prune.
4. Never invent sizes or dates.

### Forbidden Shell shapes

Multi-line scripts, many paths in one command, bare `stat`, deep walks into `venv` / `node_modules` / browser profile *contents*, Python per-file `os.stat`, parallel Shell storms.

## Default roots / bans

**Survey:** discovered `WORKSPACE`, `TMP`, `HOME` (with excludes), trash-like dirs, package/user caches, clearly orphaned empty browser profiles.

**Never candidate without an explicitly named approval:** `agent-data`, `reference`, `/proc` `/sys` `/dev` `/run`, OS system trees, live repos / manuscripts / `TEAM.md` trees. Never wipe all of temp.

## Time box

Aim for a short survey (about half a minute) when commands pass. Cap shortlist ~6.

## Classification A / B / C / D

- **A safe** (still needs approval): trash dirs, unreferenced deleted-agent remnants, tiny orphan browser profiles, reclaimable caches, old unused temp regular files (not live desktop/session sockets).
- **B judgment:** work trees, venvs, large browser profiles, tool state dirs.
- **C idle ≥ ~30 days** (info only): T = max(mtime,ctime) on work areas; note atime unreliable.
- **D uninspected:** review failures after retry, permission, timeout, missing roots.

## Delete after approval

Re-check each approved path; prefer move-to-dated-trash under `WORKSPACE` when unsure; log results; prove with `df -h /`.

## Related

Fast disk survey, Shared computer maintenance, Cheap routines.

name: Fast disk survey
description: >-
  Use when measuring disk on a shared multi-agent Linux computer with
  runtime-discovered roots and review-resilient sequential shells; pair with
  Safe disk clean.
---
# Fast disk survey

Measurement subset of Safe disk clean. No deletes.

## Discover then measure (sequential)

Resolve `HOME`, `WORKSPACE`, `TMP`, `AGENT_DATA` as in Safe disk clean. Then:

```bash
du -xhd1 "$WORKSPACE"    # if present
du -xhd1 "$TMP"
du -xhd1 --exclude=agent-data --exclude=reference "$HOME"
df -h /
ls -ld "$CANDIDATE"      # ≤6 times, one path each
ls -1 "$AGENT_DATA/agents"   # if present
```

Never bare `du -xhd1 "$HOME"` when protected dirs live under it. Never `stat`. On classifying error: retry identical command once; then mark missing.

No parallel bursts. No multi-line scripts. No deep finds into venvs / browser profile contents.

skills.name: Shared computer maintenance
skills.description: Use when cleaning, installing CLIs, or connecting services on a shared multi-agent Linux computer.
skills.content:
---
name: Shared computer maintenance
description: >-
  Use when cleaning, installing CLIs, or connecting services on a shared
  multi-agent Linux computer.
---
# Shared computer maintenance

All bots on an account share one persistent Linux computer. Files, browser logins, and installed tools persist. A desktop is per-bot; the filesystem is not.

## Inventory first

Before changing anything, list what you will touch and why. Write a short log of CLI installs under the home inventory file (name, version command, date). Do not invent disk usage numbers; measure.

## Cleanup

When Safe disk clean is present, it wins on delete policy: never delete without explicit user approval, including temp and package caches.

Never delete without an explicit go-ahead:

- `agent-data` under home (every bot's memory, routines, transcripts)
- `reference` under home
- project trees under the shared workspace that look like work (repos, manuscripts, serials, `TEAM.md`)
- anything you cannot name as junk with a measured reason (mtime, size, no references)

Unreferenced candidates: list path, size, last modified, why it looks unused. Wait for confirmation. Prefer move to a dated trash folder under the workspace over `rm -rf` when unsure.

Do not use computer Reset for cleanup. Recovery is the product's Update Computer path if the machine is broken.

## Install CLIs

- Idempotent: check `command -v` and version before install.
- Prefer distro packages or the tool's official install docs. Do not curl-pipe-to-shell unless that is the documented official method, and even then show the URL first.
- Non-interactive flags only (`-y` only when you have already named the package).
- After install, run the version command and record it in the inventory file.
- Do not install GUI-only tools that cannot run on this computer.

## External services

- Search the plugin catalog first. Prefer a connector over the browser.
- Confirm before installing a plugin (account-wide).
- Never paste tokens, passwords, or keys into chat. Use the product's secret or connect-card flow.
- Do not scrape cookies or session files to bypass auth.
- If a connector needs auth, start the connect card and stop; do not work around it.

## Proof

After cleanup or install: show the command output that proves the result (version, `df`, deleted paths). Do not claim a tool is installed without the version line.

skills.name: Cheap routines
skills.description: Use when creating or changing a bot routine, auditing bot token usage, or deciding whether recurring work belongs on a long chat or a fresh bot.
skills.content:
---
name: Cheap routines
description: >-
  Use when creating or changing a bot routine, auditing bot token usage, or
  deciding whether recurring work belongs on a long chat or a fresh bot.
---
# Cheap routines

Every scheduled wake burns tokens. Pick the coarsest cadence that still delivers the result.

## Cadence

Do not schedule every 15 minutes. That is about 96 runs a day.

Default to hourly, or a few times a day, inside weekday waking hours. Use an event listener instead of a timer when the thing you care about is a messaging or code-host event.

Stay quiet when nothing changed. Filler like "(no change.)" still costs a wake.

## Fresh bot for recurring work

A long chat makes every routine more expensive. The model rereads the thread.

Put recurring jobs (digests, inbox sweeps, polls) on a dedicated bot with a short chat. Keep talking to the main bot. That bot does not own the standing timer.

## When you create a bot

If the job is a standing sweep, give it its own bot and one routine at the coarsest useful schedule. Do not hang that routine on a bot whose chat is already long.

Quiet-when-nothing-changed is part of the job, not a courtesy.

routines.name: 週次ディスク点検
routines.description: Weekly Monday morning wake to run a quiet Safe disk clean survey and report A/B/C/D without deleting.
routines.content:
Follow Safe disk clean for a weekly disk survey. Discover HOME, WORKSPACE, and TMP each run. Sequential shells only: depth-1 du on workspace and temp, home du with agent-data and reference excluded, df on root, ls -ld on up to about six shortlisted candidates one path at a time, then list live agents if present. Never bare home-wide du or stat. On review classifying errors, retry the identical command once; otherwise mark missing and continue. Report A/B/C/D. Do not delete. Stay silent when there is nothing to report. Use the user's language; lead with the conclusion. Do not hardcode machine-specific absolute paths.

Fires on:
- cron `0 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
